title: Shifted-unit representation and edge evaluation of ringed-site hypercohomology
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring with a map $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, and let $s:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Set},A)$ be the corresponding morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Write $G=Rs_*=R\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$, with its induced $A$-action, computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], and use the canonical derived adjunction $Ls^*\dashv G$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. For $n\in\mathbf Z$, write $A_n$ and $\mathcal O_n$ for the complexes with $A$ and $\mathcal O$ respectively in degree $n$, zero elsewhere and zero differential. The canonical unit and shift comparisons give $Ls^*A_n\cong\mathcal O_n$. For every $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ there is an additive bijection, natural in $K$,
$$\gamma_K^n:H^nG(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal O_n,K).$$
It is the inverse of the canonical composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(Ls^*A_n,K)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{adj}}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(A_n,GK)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^nG(K),$$
where the last arrow evaluates the representing cocycle at $1\in A$. If $I$ is a K-injective representative of $K$ and $z$ is a degree-$n$ global cocycle in $I$, then $\gamma_K^n([z])$ is the derived class of the cochain map $\mathcal O_n\to I$ whose degree-$n$ component sends $a$ to $az$. The map $e_K^n:H^nG(K)\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal H^nK)$ taking a global cocycle in $I$ to its class in the cohomology sheaf is independent of $I$, natural for every derived morphism, and satisfies
$$e_K^n(x)=\mathcal H^n(\gamma_K^n(x))(1).$$
Here $\mathcal H^n(\mathcal O_n)=\mathcal O$, and $1$ means its compatible family of unit sections. No final site object, boundedness, flatness or enough-projectives hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), global assertion and its K-flat/K-injective proof, specialized to the shifted structure sheaf; Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology), cocycle quotient. The combined normalized statement is agent-stated.

proof.text: Apply the ringed projection/adjunction theorem to the stated morphism s to the point. Its unit identification gives Ls^*A[0] ≅ O[0], and its canonical integer-shift structures give Ls^*A_n ≅ O_n: here A_n=A[0][-n] and O_n=O[0][-n]. These are the unit and shift comparisons in the statement, not arbitrary isomorphisms between the same objects. The theorem applies to arbitrary small ringed topoi and imposes no flatness on A → Γ(O).

For any complex I of O-modules, a cochain map f:O_n → I is determined by the compatible sections z_U=f^n_U(1). Conversely a compatible family z of degree-n sections with dz=0 defines f^n_U(a)=a z_U and all other components zero. The chain-map equation is exactly dz=0. A homotopy from f_z to f_w has only one possibly nonzero component O → I^{n-1}; evaluating it at 1 gives t with z-w=d t. Conversely such t defines that homotopy by a ↦ a t. Thus evaluation and its inverse give an additive bijection H^n(Γ(I)) ≅ Hom_{K(O)}(O_n,I), natural under every cochain map I → J. These calculations use global sections as Hom_O(O,-), so they require no final object of the presented site.

source.place: Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), global computation via Tag 0A94; direct single-complex calculation of that Hom complex

proof.text: Choose a K-injective representative I of K using the existence theorem. K-injective localization identifies Hom_{K(O)}(O_n,I) with Hom_{D(O)}(O_n,K), without a boundedness condition on either complex. Compose this identification with Step 2 and the defining computation H^nG(K)=H^nΓ(I), retaining the A-action on sections. This defines γ_K^n and gives exactly the displayed representative f_z. For every derived morphism h:K → L, the K-injective derived-map theorem gives a homotopy class g:I → J which computes h and G(h). The equation g f_z=f_{g(z)} from Step 2 proves γ_L^n(H^nG(h)([z]))=h γ_K^n([z]). The same theorem's canonical resolution transitions prove independence of I; they intertwine this equation and satisfy the cocycle identity. All maps are additive.

For an arbitrary complex E of A-modules the same elementary calculation as Step 2 identifies Hom_{K(A)}(A_n,E) with H^n(E), by evaluation at 1. The complex A_n is K-projective in the definition of the cited localization theorem: if E is acyclic, any cycle z ∈ E^n is d t for some t ∈ E^{n-1}, and a ↦ a t is a null homotopy of the corresponding map. That theorem therefore identifies Hom_{D(A)}(A_n,QE) with H^n(E). It does so by the canonical localization map, so evaluation is independent of the chosen representative E and is natural for all derived morphisms. In particular this applies to E=Γ(I), which represents GK even though Γ(I) need not itself be K-injective over A.

source.place: K-projective dual of Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective); canonical localization bijection as in Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/KProjective.lean

proof.text: Use the canonical derived-adjunction normalization on the flat-term K-flat resolving class: resolutions are supplied by the K-flat resolution theorem, pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives by the supplied ringed-topos pullback theorem, and the unbounded target resolutions are those of Step 3. The complex A_n belongs to this class: its only nonzero term is free of rank one, and tensoring any acyclic complex with A_n is its degree translation with the signed differential, hence acyclic. Its pullback is the literal O_n under Step 1's unit comparison. The adjunction produced by the normalization theorem is the canonical derived adjunction of Step 1: both are induced from the ordinary module adjunction s^*⊣s_* on resolving representatives, and the normalization formula fixes the adjunction bijection Hom(Ls^*QM,QI)≅Hom(QM,G QI) for every flat-term K-flat M and K-injective I, because every derived map Ls^*QM→QI is Q of a chain map s^*M→I by K-injective localization; every object of either derived category is isomorphic to such a QM or QI by the two resolution theorems, so naturality determines the bijection everywhere and no automorphism of Ls^* can intervene. The normalization theorem says that the derived adjunct of Q(f_z):Ls^*A_n → QI is Q of its termwise adjunct A_n → Γ(I), followed by the right-derived comparison. That adjunct sends a ∈ A to its image times z; in particular 1 ↦ z. Under the K-injective computation of GK, Step 4 consequently sends this adjunct to [z]. Since every class is represented by a cocycle and γ is bijective, γ is the inverse of exactly the composite specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), normalized on representatives; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 07A6, 06YS and 0G7E

proof.text: The degree-n cohomology map of f_z sends the section a of O=H^n(O_n) to the image of a z in ker(d_I^n)/im(d_I^{n-1}), the quotient as a module sheaf. Evaluating it on the compatible family 1 therefore gives exactly the section obtained from the global cocycle z by the cohomology-sheaf quotient. A global boundary has zero image in this quotient. Thus the stated cocycle map equals x ↦ H^n(γ_K^n(x))(1). Step 3 makes γ independent of the resolution and natural for every derived morphism, and cohomology is a functor on the derived category. Applying that functor to its naturality equation proves Γ(H^n(h))(e_K^n(x))=e_L^n(H^nG(h)(x)); the same formula proves resolution independence. This establishes all edge assertions without identifying a sheaf quotient with its presheaf of sections.
